items.stem: You want to compare how 12 months of revenue change over time. Which chart type communicates the trend best?

options.rationale: Correct: line charts are designed to show change over a continuous time axis.
Pie charts show composition at one moment, not a trend.
3-D pies distort proportions and show no trend.
Like a pie, it shows parts of a whole, not change over time.

items.explanation: Correct: line charts are designed to show change over a continuous time axis.

items.stem: Which TWO practices reduce the risk of a misleading chart? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Start a bar/column value axis at zero
options.rationale: Correct: a non-zero baseline exaggerates differences between bars.

options.text: Avoid 3-D effects that distort the perception of values
options.rationale: Correct: 3-D perspective makes nearer elements look larger.

options.text: Use as many colours as possible for visual interest
options.rationale: Excess colour adds noise and can imply meaning that is not there.

options.text: Hide the axis so readers cannot question the scale
options.rationale: Removing the scale hides information rather than clarifying it.

items.explanation: Correct: a non-zero baseline exaggerates differences between bars.

items.stem: On a dashboard, one slicer should filter several PivotCharts at once. How is this achieved?

options.text: Connect the slicer to each PivotTable via Report Connections
options.rationale: Correct: a slicer can be linked to multiple pivots that share the connection.

options.text: Copy the slicer once per chart and hope they sync
options.rationale: Independent copies do not stay in sync.

options.text: Retype the filter into each chart manually
options.rationale: That defeats the purpose of an interactive control.
Chart dimensionality has nothing to do with slicer connections.

items.explanation: Correct: a slicer can be linked to multiple pivots that share the connection.
